note: SYNTHETIC fixture. Invented battery-research notes written for testing; none of these statements are real findings and the numbers must not be cited.

pages.title: Cell aging
pages.content:
## Temperature

Capacity fade accelerates above 45 degrees Celsius in the tested NMC cells.

## Calendar aging

Calendar aging is slower than cycle aging: cells stored at 25 degrees Celsius lost 4% of capacity over 12 months.

## Cycle aging

After 500 charge cycles at 1C, the NMC cells retained 88% of their initial capacity.

pages.title: Aging notes (2024)
pages.content:
Capacity fade accelerates above 60 degrees Celsius in the tested NMC cells.

After 500 charge cycles at 1C, the NMC cells retained 94% of their initial capacity.

pages.title: Fast charging
pages.content:
Charging at 3C raises the cell temperature by about 12 degrees Celsius above ambient.

Lithium plating risk rises sharply below 10 degrees Celsius during fast charging.

Pulse charging reduced plating signs in 70% of trials in the pilot study.

pages.title: Charging guidelines
pages.content:
Lithium plating risk rises sharply below 0 degrees Celsius during fast charging.

Chargers should taper current as the cell approaches full charge.

pages.title: Thermal management
pages.content:
Liquid cooling keeps pack temperature differences under 3 degrees Celsius across cells.

Air cooling is cheaper but allows temperature differences up to 10 degrees Celsius across cells.

Phase-change materials absorb heat during short peaks but do not remove it over long periods.

pages.title: Pack design
pages.content:
Liquid cooling keeps pack temperature differences under 3 degrees Celsius across cells in the reference pack.

Busbars are sized for the peak discharge current.

pages.title: Cathode chemistries
pages.content:
NMC cathodes offer higher energy density than LFP cathodes.

LFP cathodes tolerate more charge cycles; LFP cells retain 90% of capacity after 3000 cycles in laboratory tests.

Cobalt content in NMC cathodes drives cost and supply risk.

pages.title: LFP field data
pages.content:
LFP cells retain 80% of capacity after 3000 cycles in fleet operation.

Fleet duty cycles include frequent fast charging.

pages.title: Battery recycling
pages.content:
Hydrometallurgical recycling recovers over 95% of cobalt and nickel from spent cells.

Direct recycling preserves the cathode structure but needs sorted, single-chemistry input.

Collection rates remain the main bottleneck, with under 50% of spent cells reaching recyclers.

pages.title: Recycling policy
pages.content:
Policy targets require 70% of spent cells to be collected by 2030.

Producers share responsibility for end-of-life handling.

pages.title: Solid-state batteries
pages.content:
Solid-state cells replace the liquid electrolyte with a solid ceramic or polymer layer.

Prototype solid-state cells reached 400 Wh/kg in laboratory tests.

Manufacturing at scale is not expected before 2030 according to the outlook.

pages.title: Energy density trends (2024)
pages.content:
Commercial lithium-ion cells reach about 250 Wh/kg in 2024.

Solid-state cells are not expected to exceed 300 Wh/kg in laboratory tests.

pages.title: Battery safety
pages.content:
Thermal runaway typically begins above 150 degrees Celsius inside the cell.

Venting gas from a failing cell is flammable and toxic.

Separators with ceramic coating delay internal short circuits.
